result.summary: Manual review of the draft/dirty-guard slice only: `src/shared/connection-manager/draft.ts`, the Kotlin `ConnectionDraft.kt`, `ConnectionDraftTest.kt` and the Kotlin-draft parity test. I found one LOW defect: the TypeScript draft leaks compiled Ajv validators. I found no reachable correctness, privacy, or dirty-guard defect in the supplied code. The TS and Kotlin drafts mirror each other for identity fixing, Keep/Replace/Clear credential intents, reset-to-baseline, unsafe-field rejection, and a Cancel that has zero effect. Discard clears only the unsaved draft. Most assigned obligations cover files that were not supplied (extension.ts, the Settings configurable, plugin.xml, the manager models/panels, the IPC lanes, removal, test wiring), so they are `could-not-verify`. This is not a canonical CR and does not approve BUILD.

findings.trigger: Open Create or Edit forms repeatedly, or re-render the kind list, in a long-lived VS Code workbench.
findings.defect: `validators()` calls `ajv.compile()` on freshly built schema objects every time, using a single module-level `Ajv` instance. The constructor deep-copies the descriptor with `data(descriptor)`, and `editingSchema()` builds a new object on every call. I believe Ajv caches compiled schemas by schema-object identity in a strong internal Map. If so, no call ever hits the cache, and every `new ConnectionDraft` and every `connectionDriverChoices` call leaves compiled validators in the shared instance. `connectionDriverChoices` compiles two validators for each of about 29 descriptors per call.
findings.evidence: Line 29 creates one module-level `ajv`. Line 58 compiles `descriptor.publicInputSchema` and `editingSchema(descriptor.publicInputSchema)`. The constructor passes `freeze(data(descriptor))` to `validators`, so its schema objects are new on every call. Nothing calls `ajv.removeSchema` or keys validators by kind. The Ajv cache behaviour is my knowledge of the library, not shown in the supplied evidence.
findings.remedy: Cache the `{full, editing}` pair by a stable key (kind plus JSON of the schema) in a bounded Map. Alternatively, remove the compiled schema with `ajv.removeSchema(schema)` after use, or use a short-lived `Ajv` per draft.

obligations.evidence: The scope-correction call sites (`vscode-plugin/src/extension.ts`, `InsrcSettingsConfigurable.kt`) were not supplied. The supplied files stay within `src/shared` and `jetbrains-plugin` and add no deprecated-fork dependency.
This covers ConnectionListState, the Settings and command entry points, and plugin.xml. None of those files, and no list-state code, were supplied.

The shared serializer is present in `serialize()` for TS and Kotlin and is memory-only, with a `draftRevision` increment on every edit. Test/cancel/in-flight/stale-result identity wiring and `extension.ts` were not supplied.
Removal state and `connection-removal.ts` were not supplied. The draft layer only models a `remove` navigation target that is guarded by the dirty check.

The project-scoped service, panel, plugin.xml and EDT/disposal guards were not supplied. `ConnectionDraft.kt` is pure Gson/JDK code with no IntelliJ SDK, global project or PersistentStateComponent use, and its fields are @Transient.
`serialize()` carries `expectedRevision` on update. Busy/conflict handling, reconfirm and the retained operation card were not supplied.
List, filter and count state were not supplied.

At the draft layer this holds. `requestExit` stores a pending target when the draft is dirty. A Cancel clears it with no effect and leaves the values and revision unchanged. A Discard clears only the unsaved inputs and returns the navigate effect. The Kotlin test covers eight target types. Wiring in the manager and panel-close handling was not supplied.
`draft.ts` imports only Ajv and shared pure modules, and the Kotlin draft is likewise pure. The rest of the client core was not supplied.
The draft serializer shape is consistent with sc4 inputs (key, expectedRevision, publicPatch, credentials). The IPC and daemon side were not supplied.
The supplied files show no re-implementation of backend contracts. The full change set was not supplied.
`ConnectionProtocol.kt` and its decoder tests were not supplied. `ConnectionDraft.kt` only consumes `ConnectionProtocol.publicPatch`, `requestData`, `decodePublicPercent` and the descriptors.
`ConnectionsManagerModel.kt` and the state transcripts were not supplied.

`draft.ts` implements all three acceptance checks. `connectionDriverChoices` enables or disables each kind with guidance. Identity is fixed on edit. Credential intents are Keep/Replace/Clear and masked. A dirty exit needs Discard or Cancel. The CM-S5-FORM-TS test file was not among the supplied files. The LOW validator-cache finding applies to this file.
Test/cancel wiring, one-in-flight probe and stale-result suppression were not supplied.
Delete/Discard presentation and ticket-only retry were not supplied.
Live JetBrains UI acceptance is deferred by the user and there was no evidence to review.

limitations: Only the four files listed were supplied. I did not see wire.ts, connection-management-wire.ts, ConnectionProtocol.kt, the corpus fixtures, or the callers of the draft.

The TS and Kotlin schema validators may differ for descriptors that omit additionalProperties:false. Kotlin always rejects undeclared keys, and Ajv allows them. I could not confirm this from the supplied descriptors, so I did not raise it as a defect.
The Kotlin draft invokes `onChange` listeners while holding its object lock. I saw no listener implementation, so I could not tell whether a deadlock is reachable.
I did not run any tests, so the claimed 4 JUnit tests and the 29-descriptor assertion are unverified.
The LOW finding relies on how Ajv caches compiled schemas internally, which was not in the supplied evidence.
evidenceRequests: connection-manager/wire.ts and ConnectionProtocol.kt, to confirm decoder parity, strict percent decoding and the descriptor shape guarantees (a nested `properties` is always present).
The ConnectionDraft call sites in the manager host and panel (listener threading, how Test uses `serialize`).
